elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "All results of the Support Services and any other materials, work product or deliverables prepared by TrueLink for Client under this Agreement shall be the exclusive property of Client"

elements.element: Vendor assigns such rights to Customer
elements.evidence: "TrueLink hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest therein"
"TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface" (untouched Section 2(d))

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "to the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded in such results, TrueLink grants Client a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use the same as part of such results"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "Client retains all right, title and interest in and to the Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, the Credit Data and all other data submitted by or on behalf of Client or its customers"
"no item is jointly owned by the parties"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: No reference to generic tools or know-how; only "ownership and license rights in the Interface"

elements.element: Perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to deliverables
elements.evidence: Licence is limited to embedded Vendor IP and omits "worldwide": "perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to use the same as part of such results"

elements.element: Right to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for Customer's business
elements.evidence: Only "license to use the same as part of such results" — no modification or sublicensing rights

reasons: The inserted Section 2(e) completes every atomic element of the preferred position: Customer ownership of results/work product/deliverables with an express Vendor assignment, a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any embedded Vendor IP, retention of all rights in Client Content/IP/data, and an express no-joint-ownership statement.
Vendor's pre-existing IP retention is preserved by the untouched Section 2(d) ownership of the Interface, so the preferred bargain is intact without duplicating protection.

Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (no generic tools/know-how ownership statement and no worldwide use/modify/sublicense licence over deliverables), but that is irrelevant because the locked preferred level is met and the levels are separate bargains.
Minimality holds: a single concise insertion addressing an absent Customer-ownership clause, with no rewrite of the confidentiality or term provisions and no fallback-only wording imported.
Intent preserved: the carve-out "(subject only to the license granted in Section 8(d))" keeps the existing Vendor licence effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
